title: AI document workflow platforms: Decision Brief
executive_summary: AI document workflow platforms: coverage 1/3 primary questions, 5 recommendation-safe claims, contradiction count 0.
decision_context: Choose a primary platform for a production pilot in the next two quarters.
key_findings: Glean is strongest when the core problem is knowledge access across enterprise tools and permissions. [Evidence: a5d07fc3-85a3-4091-88e3-4af93c5dcdb3, 1afbc477-e6f0-4343-a0ea-f328b05a6474]

Its value is connector breadth and enterprise search positioning more than deep document workflow automation inside one content system. [Evidence: a0dd0eb5-16e6-4d60-9617-c1b2c78664d7, 386d393d-ed1b-4055-a22b-3ca5503e0fca]

Box AI makes the strongest case where controlled document workflows and governance inside an existing content platform are the priority. [Evidence: ca80eb20-6788-4bd3-b437-b75d438a71f3, 1d54d0ef-a542-4fdc-a654-154bc076b9ad]

Notion AI is compelling when user adoption and low-friction workspace assistance matter more than heavyweight governance or cross-enterprise retrieval. [Evidence: 462c2fc1-de49-4cec-8ee6-8bf3f05b79f3, ae586ad4-6c35-436e-ab60-79ae08b61eac]
It is strongest as a productivity layer, not as the single system of record for complex document operations. [Evidence: 887a3468-3d79-4721-9dba-a1f744ed91a3, 4d95feab-ae16-41d4-8f26-cac452c72627]
key_risks: Prefer pragmatic operating cost and privacy-aware deployment.
limitations: Where does integration breadth matter more than model sophistication?
What are the main adoption and governance risks?
uncertainty_statement: Recommendations are bounded because the evidence base is incomplete.
